recent_posts.title: Cushman & Wakefield confirms vishing cyberattack
recent_posts.summary: Real estate firm Cushman & Wakefield has confirmed a data breach caused by a vishing (voice phishing) attack. Two separate cybercrime groups, ShinyHunters and Qilin, have independently claimed responsibility. ShinyHunters alleges it stole over 500,000 Salesforce records containing PII, with a May 6 deadline for the company to make contact or face a data leak. Qilin, considered the world's most prolific ransomware group, listed C&W on its leak site separately. The incident is part of ShinyHunters' broader campaign that began in March after breaching Salesforce customers, with victims including ADT, Carnival Cruise Line, Rockstar Games, and Vimeo.

recent_posts.title: Five Eyes warn agentic is too dangerous for rapid rollout
recent_posts.summary: Five Eyes intelligence agencies (CISA, NSA, NCSC-UK, ACSC, and others) have jointly published guidance warning that agentic AI systems pose significant security risks and should be adopted slowly and carefully. The document highlights how agentic AI expands attack surfaces through interconnected components, tools, and data sources. It provides concrete examples of how overly permissive agents can be exploited — such as a malicious insider using a patch-management agent to delete firewall logs, or an attacker compromising a low-risk tool to inherit an agent's broad financial system privileges. The agencies list 23 distinct risks and over 100 best practices, urging organizations to prioritize resilience and human oversight over efficiency, deploy incrementally starting with low-risk tasks, and assume agentic AI will behave unexpectedly until security standards mature.

recent_posts.title: AI-BOMs replace SBOMs as way to track AI agents and bots
recent_posts.summary: As AI agents, models, and tools proliferate in enterprise environments, traditional SBOMs no longer provide sufficient inventory coverage. AI-BOMs extend the concept to include models, datasets, MCP servers, ML frameworks, agentic skills, prompts, and their interconnections. Cisco has open-sourced both an AI-BOM scanner and a new Model Provenance Kit that uses metadata and weight-based signals to verify model lineage — relevant for regulatory compliance like the EU AI Act. Google's Wiz extends AI-BOMs to cover developer tooling and non-human identities tied to AI workloads. Real-world incidents show attackers exploiting gaps in AI visibility, including modifying system prompts to exfiltrate data. AI-BOMs also help detect supply chain attacks like poisoned npm/PyPI packages and tampered AI skills by tracking state changes and enabling rapid identification of compromised components.

recent_posts.title: Public voter records can expose personal data when linked
recent_posts.summary: Research by Noah Kenney demonstrates that publicly available voter records from Texas and North Carolina can be cross-referenced with other public datasets — such as FEC contribution data and social media — to re-identify individuals at high rates, even when certain fields are redacted. Using a simple Python script and no fuzzy matching, 52% of voters were uniquely identified from just two datasets; commercial data broker tools could push that to 90–95%. Key findings include that name and ZIP alone identify over 95% of Texas voters, long voting histories act as fingerprints, and 320 deployed military families are exposed via APO/FPO codes. Kenney recommends access controls, rate limiting, identity verification, audit logs, and opt-out rights over field redaction, while noting that proposed federal privacy legislation is unlikely to pass.

recent_posts.title: Kids can bypass some age checks with a drawn-on mustache
recent_posts.summary: A UK survey of over 1,000 children and parents reveals that age verification measures introduced under the Online Safety Act are largely ineffective. Some 46% of children say age checks are easy to bypass, using methods ranging from entering fake birthdays and using others' ID cards to using video game characters to fool selfie systems — and in some cases, simply drawing a mustache on their face. About 32% admit to actually bypassing checks. Compounding the problem, 17% of parents actively help their children evade age gates, while 9% turn a blind eye. Nearly half of surveyed children (49%) report encountering harmful content online recently, suggesting age gates are failing even those who don't actively circumvent them. Internet Matters CEO Rachel Huggins called for stronger action from both government and industry to build safety into online services from the outset.

recent_posts.title: NCSC warns AI is accelerating discovery of legacy code vulnerabilities
recent_posts.summary: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) is warning organizations to prepare for a 'patch tsunami' as AI-powered tools rapidly uncover decades of accumulated technical debt and buried vulnerabilities. NCSC CTO Ollie Whitehouse warns that AI is exposing weaknesses at scale and pace, likely triggering a forced correction across the technology ecosystem. Organizations are urged to minimize their internet-facing attack surfaces, prioritize perimeter technologies, and prepare to patch quickly and at scale. The same AI tools being marketed to defenders — such as Anthropic's Claude Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber — also lower the barrier for attackers to find vulnerabilities.

recent_posts.title: Home Office adds £216M to travel doc contract before bids
recent_posts.summary: The UK Home Office has increased its upcoming passport production contract from £360 million to £576 million (including VAT) and extended its duration from 10 to 12 years, raising the annual value from £36 million to £48 million. The contract start date has been pushed back a year to August 2028, and the full tender notice publication has been delayed from June to November 2025. HM Passport Office now issues around eight million passports annually, up from seven million. The new supplier will handle physical passport production, personalisation with biometric data, and potentially digital travel credentials and crypto technologies. Separately, the Home Office is paying IBM £5.88 million for proprietary biometric software licenses and support, awarded without competition due to no viable alternative.

recent_posts.title: Critical cPanel zero-day actively exploited with ransomware attacks reported
recent_posts.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in cPanel and WHM (CVE-2026-41940, CVSS 9.8) is being actively exploited, with CISA adding it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Exploitation began before patches were available, with one hosting provider reporting attack attempts as early as February 2026. Namecheap temporarily blocked cPanel access, and at least one small business reports a $7,000 ransomware demand following compromise. Roughly 1.5 million internet-exposed cPanel instances were identified via Shodan, with tens of millions of websites potentially at risk. Users are urged to patch immediately and assume compromise if systems were left unpatched.

recent_posts.title: OpenAI restricts GPT-5.5-Cyber access weeks after mocking Anthropic for the same
recent_posts.summary: OpenAI is preparing a restricted release of GPT-5.5-Cyber, a model capable of pentesting, bug finding, exploit development, and malware analysis, to a select group of trusted cyber defenders. The move is notable because Sam Altman recently criticized Anthropic for doing nearly the same thing with its Claude Mythos model, calling such exclusivity 'fear-based marketing.' The UK's AI Security Institute independently confirmed GPT-5.5-Cyber is among the strongest models tested on cyber tasks, being only the second to complete a multi-step attack simulation end to end.

recent_posts.title: Pro-Iran group turns Ubuntu DDoS into shakedown
recent_posts.summary: Pro-Iranian hacktivist group 313 Team (Islamic Cyber Resistance in Iraq) launched a sustained DDoS attack against Canonical's web infrastructure, taking down ubuntu.com and many subdomains for over 12 hours. The group, which initially announced a four-hour attack window via Telegram, has since escalated to extortion, demanding Canonical contact them or face continued assault. Users are unable to download Ubuntu distros or access Canonical accounts through normal channels. The group has also claimed recent DDoS attacks against eBay Japan, eBay US, and BlueSky.
